react_result.final_narrative_text: Three orthogonal pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: the arachidonic acid eicosanoid cascade. The multi-database ORA (RaMP) places WikiPathways "Eicosanoid synthesis" (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked entry across Reactome, SMPDB, KEGG and WikiPathways with FDR = 3.1e-15 and a fold enrichment of ~2001x, annotating five of the eight input metabolites (arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2, 15-HETE, and leukotriene A4). The KEGG-specific PSEA (MetaboAnalystR) independently recovers KEGG:hsa00590 (arachidonic acid metabolism) as the sole significant pathway at p = 2.5e-06, with the same four eicosanoid intermediates (arachidonic acid, LTA4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE) driving the hit. The m/z-direct network method (Mummichog) confirms three sub-pathways at its top ranks: "Arachidonic acid metabolism" (p = 1.7e-4), "Leukotriene metabolism" (p = 2.5e-2), and "Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate" (p = 3.5e-2), using the empirical human_mfn compound graph. 5,6-EET also appears within the full arachidonic acid network hit from Mummichog. The two aromatic metabolites (3,4-dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid) are absent from all top-ranked eicosanoid pathways across the three paradigms, indicating they are peripheral signals not integrated into the core arachidonate cascade. Arachidonic acid is the primary substrate driving the entire observed signal; it is metabolised via cyclooxygenases (producing 15-deoxy-PGJ2) and lipoxygenases (producing 5-HETE, 15-HETE and the leukotriene A4 branch), consistent with simultaneous multi-arm pathway activation in the treatment group.

  "narrative_text": "Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on the eicosanoid synthesis cascade in this metabolomics dataset. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three orthogonal pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: the arachidonic acid eicosanoid cascade. The multi-database ORA (RaMP) places WikiPathways "Eicosanoid synthesis" (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked entry across Reactome, SMPDB, KEGG and WikiPathways with FDR = 3.1e-15 and a fold enrichment of ~2001x, annotating five of the eight input metabolites (arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2, 15-HETE, and leukotriene A4). The KEGG-specific PSEA (MetaboAnalystR) independently recovers KEGG:hsa00590 (arachidonic acid metabolism) as the sole significant pathway at p = 2.5e-06, with the same four eicosanoid intermediates (arachidonic acid, LTA4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE) driving the hit. The m/z-direct network method (Mummichog) confirms three sub-pathways at its top ranks: "Arachidonic acid metabolism" (p = 1.7e-4), "Leukotriene metabolism" (p = 2.5e-2), and "Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate" (p = 3.5e-2), using the empirical human_mfn compound graph. 5,6-EET also appears within the full arachidonic acid network hit from Mummichog. The two aromatic metabolites (3,4-dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid) are absent from all top-ranked eicosanoid pathways across the three paradigms, indicating they are peripheral signals not integrated into the core arachidonate cascade. Arachidonic acid is the primary substrate driving the entire observed signal; it is metabolised via cyclooxygenases (producing 15-deoxy-PGJ2) and lipoxygenases (producing 5-HETE, 15-HETE and the leukotriene A4 branch), consistent with simultaneous multi-arm pathway activation in the treatment group.
